note: One line per cue in store/promo/video/apq-debugger-demo-cues.json, in order. Spelled for the TTS ("Graph Q L", "A-P-Q" — a lone "A" is read as the article, "U R L"; lowercase "curl" so it is read as a word, not C-U-R-L).
lines: Graph Q L Debugger. Pause, edit and read every request.
With Automatic Persisted Queries, Apollo sends a hash instead of the query, so the Network panel can't show what ran.
First, tell Graph Q L Debugger which requests to watch.
Press Start. The yellow bar stays up while requests are being rewritten.
Each hash is swapped, the server asks for the full query, and Apollo retries. The row resolves in place.
Open any operation to read and copy the full query, and its variables.
Copy it as a curl command, with the headers captured from the page, and replay it from a terminal.
Set a breakpoint on an operation name, and matching requests pause before they're sent.
Edit the query, variables or headers, then resume. Only the request waits. The page keeps running.
Filter by name, U R L, or request type.
On the Schema tab, load the schema by introspection, reusing headers from live traffic.
Stop when you're done. Nothing from your traffic leaves your browser.
Graph Q L Debugger. Breakpoints, A-P-Q, and schema.
